objective: Find multi-agent scientific-discovery patterns that shorten Phase-1 feasibility proof and decomposition.

slice.question: Is there public benchmark evidence that role-specialized scientific agents coordinated through a persistent research state are a credible decomposition pattern for scientific-discovery work?

problem_count_forecast.forecast_note: This slice resolves existence/benchmark plausibility only; causal attribution of gains to the multi-agent decomposition remains one explicit child problem.

direct_solution_first.reason: A public primary paper reports a specialized multi-agent scientific workflow with strong system-level BixBench results, but the evidence available in the primary abstract does not isolate the contribution of role specialization or persistent state from model/tool-stack effects.

candidate_pattern.name: role-specialized agents plus persistent research state and selective human checkpoints
components: persistent world state across research cycles
semi-autonomous mode with selective human checkpoints
candidate_pattern.clean_boundary_note: This is an external design pattern candidate only. It does not authorize scientist_agents to consume other workers, downstream state, O, legacy state, or a shared exploration ledger.

public_primary_evidence.source: Rethinking the AI Scientist: Interactive Multi-Agent Workflows for Scientific Discovery
observations: The reported architecture uses specialized agents for planning, data analysis, literature search, and novelty detection coordinated through a persistent world state.
The paper reports 48.8% open-response accuracy and 64.5% multiple-choice accuracy on BixBench, with a reported improvement of 14 to 26 percentage points over cited baselines.
The paper explicitly identifies open-access literature limitations and automated novelty-assessment challenges as deployment constraints.

public_primary_evidence.source: BixBench: a Comprehensive Benchmark for LLM-based Agents in Computational Biology
observations: BixBench contains more than 50 real-world biological data-analysis scenarios and nearly 300 open-answer questions requiring multi-step analysis and interpretation.

The original benchmark paper reports frontier-model agent performance of 17% accuracy in the open-answer regime, establishing that the benchmark is materially challenging rather than a near-saturated test.

benchmark_assessment.positive_signal: The reported Deep Research system-level open-response score is 48.8% on a benchmark whose original frontier-agent baseline was 17%.
benchmark_assessment.scope_limit: The compared values come from different system vintages/configurations; this slice treats them as evidence that the task is difficult and that the newer system is competitive, not as a controlled causal estimate of the multi-agent architecture.

negative_evidence_and_limits: The primary Deep Research abstract reports system-level benchmark scores but no component ablation that isolates role specialization, persistent state, or human checkpoints; causal attribution to the multi-agent decomposition is therefore unverified in this slice.
The same primary source flags limitations from open-access literature coverage and automated novelty assessment.

The exact published system may rely on model/API/tool resources that are not admissible under the Phase-1 zero-finite-quota/zero-incremental-cost gate; only the coordination pattern is being considered here, not its provider stack.

A persistent shared world state would violate this role's CLEAN input boundary if implemented as a cross-worker exploration ledger; any later adaptation must preserve role-local independence and use only sanitized handoff mechanisms authorized by repository control.

inference.candidate_value: Role specialization appears credible as a decomposition template for separating planning, evidence retrieval, analysis, novelty checking, and human-gated review, which can reduce ambiguity in assigning scientific subproblems and verification responsibilities.
inference.why_not_high: No controlled ablation was established here, and resource admissibility of the published implementation is not proven.

decomposition_on_failure.child_problem: Determine whether controlled evidence or an ablation shows that specialist-role decomposition and/or persistent state improves scientific-task accuracy, reliability, or elapsed time versus a matched single-agent or simpler orchestration baseline.

transversal_on_overrun.reason: Observed active problem count did not exceed the one-leaf forecast during this bounded slice.

expected_completion_forecast.next_slice_target: Find a primary controlled comparison or ablation for multi-agent scientific role decomposition; if absent, record non-attribution as negative evidence and test an alternative verification-centric pattern.

alternative_method_on_overrun.fallback: If no controlled architecture attribution is found next time, compare a verifier/critic-only scientific workflow against role-specialized multi-agent orchestration using primary benchmark evidence.

handoff_target: integrator via CLEAN safe summaries only
continuation: Next invocation: audit primary controlled comparisons or ablations that isolate the effect of specialist-role decomposition and persistent research state on scientific-task quality or elapsed time, while preserving the CLEAN boundary and zero-cost/quota admissibility gate.
